fullPassage:
Wheels of Adventures

A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, feeling excited and a little scared that I was traveling without my parents. My only companions would be my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair. I wasn't sure what kinds of challenges we would face, but Dan assured me that we would be the coolest travelers in Northern California. When we finally landed in San Francisco, the Golden Gate City, Dan shouted, "Let's get rolling!"

Known for its rolling hills, the city has an extensive public transportation system. I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars, which I had been looking forward to riding, do not accommodate wheelchair users. Therefore, we decided to take a city tour bus with wheelchair access. When Dan and I got on the bus, the friendly driver welcomed us aboard, and we were off.

Fisherman's Wharf is popular for its pretty shops and seafood restaurants. We were hungry, but it took almost an hour for us to look around and decide what to eat for lunch. We chose to eat a roasted crab and clam chowder soup. The sea lions peacefully lying on the floats near the pier looked like melting chocolate. They didn't smell pleasant up close, yet their cuteness delayed our visit to the Golden Gate Bridge, the famous spot that appears in most movies and TV shows filmed in San Francisco. We took a cruise, enjoying the view of the city. As we passed the bridge, the summer breeze blew slowly, and we watched the beautiful sunset.

The next day, we traveled to Yosemite National Park, a place four hours away from San Francisco and about five times bigger than Seoul. The park is famous for Northern California's natural scenery of grand waterfalls, valleys, and countless forests. Dan's uncle Roy, who lives in San Francisco, kindly gave us a ride to the park. While heading east in his car, we saw the scenery gradually changing from city to suburb, to forest, and finally, to mountain. By lunchtime, we arrived at the park, and each of us had a giant hamburger to fuel up for a hike.

While exploring a trail in Yosemite, we stopped frequently to appreciate the fresh air blowing through the giant sequoias. We passed some famous trees like the Grizzly Giant, which is about 63.7 meters tall and is almost 3,000 years old. It was massive, and I felt quite small in comparison.

Our hike took a dangerous turn at one point. As we made our way down a trail, we encountered a black bear. I was so excited that I took out my camera to take a picture. It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips we had packed because it began to approach us. Thinking quickly, Uncle Roy grabbed a stone and threw it, yelling and waving. After turning me around, Dan helped Uncle Roy push me back the way we came. Dan said, "I guess it's time to leave now." That wasn't a problem because I had gotten my picture!

Another memorable part of the trip was the bike ride. Dan found out that the National Park has a bike rental service and offers hand-crank bikes. Dan persuaded me to try one, and soon I was able to use the hand crank pretty well. We had a fun day riding along the trails in the park. The Tunnel View in Yosemite Valley was like a masterpiece painted by Mother Nature. The trail also led us to green fields and streams where we saw some wildlife. Watching people floating down the Merced River and hiking the Half Dome was cool. It was indeed a wonderful trip, with lots of laughter, joy, and sweat.

I am now in my room where I am organizing hundreds of photos, including one of the bottom half of a black bear to post on social media. Of course, I have valuable memories too. I was fortunate to have companions like Dan and Uncle Roy during the trip. There were obstacles to overcome and challenges to meet, but what adventure doesn't? I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges. All I needed to take with me was courage. I am already looking forward to my next trip in the future.

questions.passage: Fisherman's Wharf is popular for its pretty shops and seafood restaurants. We were hungry, but it took almost an hour for us ①<u>to look</u> around and decide what to eat for lunch. We chose to eat a roasted crab and clam chowder soup. The sea lions peacefully ②<u>lying</u> on the floats near the pier ③<u>looked</u> like melting chocolate. They didn't smell ④<u>pleasantly</u> up close.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 그들은 가까이에서 쾌적한(pleasant) 냄새가 나지 않았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ pleasantly → pleasant: 감각동사 smell 뒤에는 부사가 아닌 형용사가 와야 함
❌ ① to look: 'it took ~ for us to look' 가주어 구문. 정상
❌ ② lying: 현재분사, sea lions 수식. 정상
❌ ③ looked: '~처럼 보이다' 연결동사. 정상
det.tip: 감각동사(look/smell/taste/feel/sound) + 형용사(보어). 부사 사용은 오류

questions.passage: The next day, we traveled to Yosemite National Park, a place four hours away from San Francisco and about five times ①<u>bigger</u> than Seoul. The park is famous for Northern California's natural scenery of grand waterfalls, valleys, and countless forests. Dan's uncle Roy, ②<u>who</u> lives in San Francisco, kindly gave us a ride to the park. While ③<u>heading</u> east in his car, we saw the scenery gradually ④<u>change</u> from city to suburb, to forest, and finally, to mountain.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 우리는 풍경이 도시에서 교외로, 숲으로, 마지막으로 산으로 점차 변하는 것을(changing) 보았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ change → changing: 지각동사 saw + 목적어 + 현재분사(~ing). 풍경이 변하는 과정을 목격했으므로 진행 의미의 changing
❌ ① bigger: 'five times bigger than'은 배수 비교급 표현. 정상
❌ ② who: 관계대명사 계속적 용법, 선행사 Uncle Roy(사람). 정상
❌ ③ heading: 접속사 while + 분사구문. 정상
det.tip: 지각동사 + O + ~ing(진행)/원형(완료): 'saw the scenery changing'은 변화의 과정을 목격. gradually(서서히)가 진행 단서

questions.passage: I am now in my room where I am organizing hundreds of photos, ①<u>including</u> one of the bottom half of a black bear to post on social media. Of course, I have valuable memories too. I was fortunate ②<u>to have</u> companions like Dan and Uncle Roy during the trip. There were obstacles to overcome and challenges ③<u>to meet</u>, but what adventure doesn't? I took a deep breath, ④<u>dived</u> into a new world, and faced challenges.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 나는 심호흡을 하고, 새로운 세계에 뛰어들었다(dove).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ dived → dove: dive의 과거형은 dove(미국식)/dived(영국식) 모두 가능하지만, 원문은 dove 사용. 'took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced'에서 병렬구조(took-dove-faced)
❌ ① including: 전치사적 용법, '~을 포함하여'. 정상
❌ ② to have: 'was fortunate to have' 형용사 + to부정사. 정상
❌ ③ to meet: 'challenges to meet' to부정사의 형용사적 용법. 정상
det.tip: dive-dove-dived(미국식) / dive-dived-dived(영국식). 병렬구조에서 시제 통일 확인: took, dove, faced 모두 과거형

questions.passage: Known for its rolling hills, the city has an ①<u>extensive</u> public transportation system. I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars, which I had been looking forward to riding, do not ②<u>accommodate</u> wheelchair users. Therefore, we decided to take a city tour bus with wheelchair ③<u>access</u>. When Dan and I got on the bus, the ④<u>hostile</u> driver welcomed us aboard, and we were off.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 친절한(friendly) 운전사가 우리를 환영했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ hostile(적대적인) → friendly(친절한): 'welcomed us aboard'(환영했다)와 hostile은 모순
❌ ① extensive(광범위한): 대중교통 시스템을 묘사. 원문 그대로
❌ ② accommodate(수용하다): 케이블카의 휠체어 접근성. 원문 그대로
❌ ③ access(접근): wheelchair access. 원문 그대로
det.tip: friendly(친절한) ↔ hostile(적대적인). 'welcomed'(환영했다)가 friendly의 단서

questions.passage: Another memorable part of the trip was the bike ride. Dan found out that the National Park has a bike rental service and offers hand-crank bikes. Dan ①<u>persuaded</u> me to try one, and soon I was able to use the hand crank pretty well. We had a fun day riding along the trails in the park. The Tunnel View in Yosemite Valley was like a masterpiece painted by Mother Nature. The trail also led us to green fields and streams where we saw some ②<u>wildlife</u>. Watching people floating down the Merced River and hiking the Half Dome was cool. It was indeed a ③<u>wonderful</u> trip, with lots of laughter, joy, and sweat. I am now in my room where I am organizing hundreds of photos to post on social media. Of course, I have ④<u>worthless</u> memories too.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 물론, 나는 소중한(valuable) 추억도 가지고 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ worthless(가치 없는) → valuable(가치 있는): 'Of course'(물론)와 함께 긍정적 추억을 강조하는 맥락에서 worthless는 반의어
❌ ① persuaded(설득했다): Dan이 설득한 원문 그대로
❌ ② wildlife(야생동물): 들판과 시냇가의 야생동물. 원문 그대로
❌ ③ wonderful(멋진): 웃음, 기쁨, 땀의 여행. 원문 그대로
det.tip: valuable(가치 있는) ↔ worthless(가치 없는). 'Of course'가 긍정적 맥락의 단서

questions.passage: Our hike took a dangerous turn at one point. As we made our way down a trail, we encountered a black bear. I was so excited that I took out my camera to take a picture. It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips we had packed because it began to approach us. Thinking quickly, Uncle Roy __________, yelling and waving.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: grabbed a stone and threw it

det.korean: Roy 삼촌은 빠르게 생각하고 돌을 집어 던졌다(grabbed a stone and threw it).
det.analysis:
✅ ② grabbed a stone and threw it: 원문 그대로. 곰을 쫓기 위해 돌을 던지며 소리 지름
❌ ① ran away in panic: 소리 지르고 손을 흔든다는 것은 대항하는 것이지 도망이 아님
❌ ③ called the park rangers: 즉각적 대응이 필요한 상황에 전화하는 것은 부적합
❌ ④ offered the bear some food: 곰에게 음식을 주는 것은 위험
det.tip: 'Thinking quickly(빠르게 생각하며)'가 즉각적 대응의 단서. yelling and waving과 함께 곰을 쫓는 행동

questions.passage: I was fortunate to have companions like Dan and Uncle Roy during the trip. There were obstacles to overcome and challenges to meet, but what adventure doesn't? I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges. All I needed to take with me was __________. I am already looking forward to my next trip in the future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 내가 가져가야 할 전부는 용기(courage)뿐이었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ courage(용기): 장애물 극복, 새 세계 도전, 다음 여행 기대의 맥락
❌ ① a detailed plan(세부 계획): 교훈적 메시지와 어울리지 않음
❌ ② professional help(전문 도움): 'All I needed'(내가 필요한 전부)와 어울리지 않음
❌ ④ expensive equipment(비싼 장비): 물질이 아닌 마음가짐의 맥락
det.tip: 'dove into a new world'(새 세계로 뛰어들다)와 'faced challenges'(도전에 맞서다)가 courage의 핵심 단서

questions.passage: A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, feeling excited and a little scared that I was traveling without my parents. My only companions would be my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair. When we finally landed in San Francisco, the Golden Gate City, Dan shouted, "Let's get rolling!"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 나의 유일한 동반자(companions)는 가장 친한 친구 Dan과 내 휠체어(wheelchair)였다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① Dan과 휠체어: 'My only companions would be my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair' 원문 일치
❌ ② 부모님 없이: 'without my parents'
❌ ③ 샌프란시스코: 'landed in San Francisco'
❌ ④ Dan은 신나서: 'Let's get rolling!'이라고 외침
det.tip: companions(동반자)의 구체적 대상을 정확히 파악

questions.passage: Fisherman's Wharf is popular for its pretty shops and seafood restaurants. We were hungry, but it took almost an hour for us to look around and decide what to eat for lunch. We chose to eat a roasted crab and clam chowder soup. The sea lions peacefully lying on the floats near the pier looked like melting chocolate.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 피셔맨스 와프는 예쁜 가게와 해산물 식당으로 유명하다.
점심 메뉴를 정하는 데 거의 한 시간이 걸렸다.
글쓴이는 구운 게와 클램 차우더 수프를 먹었다.
바다사자들은 부두 위에서 활발하게 뛰어다니고 있었다.

det.korean: 바다사자들은 부두 근처 부표 위에 평화롭게 누워(peacefully lying) 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 활발하게 뛰어다닌다: 'peacefully lying'(평화롭게 누워있는)이므로 불일치
❌ ① 예쁜 가게와 해산물: 'pretty shops and seafood restaurants' 일치
❌ ② 거의 한 시간: 'almost an hour' 일치
❌ ③ 구운 게와 차우더: 'roasted crab and clam chowder soup' 일치
det.tip: peacefully lying(평화롭게 누워있는) ≠ 활발하게 뛰어다니는. 행동 묘사 변조가 함정

questions.passage: Our hike took a dangerous turn at one point. As we made our way down a trail, we encountered a black bear. I was so excited that I took out my camera to take a picture. It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips we had packed because it began to approach us. Thinking quickly, Uncle Roy grabbed a stone and threw it, yelling and waving. After turning me around, Dan helped Uncle Roy push me back the way we came. Dan said, "I guess it's time to leave now." That wasn't a problem because I had gotten my picture!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 글쓴이는 곰 사진을 찍는 데 성공했다.

det.korean: 글쓴이는 너무 신나서(so excited) 카메라를 꺼내 사진을 찍었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 겁에 질려 카메라를 떨어뜨렸다: 'so excited that I took out my camera'이므로 흥분해서 사진을 찍은 것. 불일치
❌ ① 오솔길에서 곰 만남: 'made our way down a trail, we encountered a black bear' 일치
❌ ③ Roy 삼촌의 돌: 'grabbed a stone and threw it' 일치
❌ ④ 사진 성공: 'I had gotten my picture' 일치
det.tip: excited(흥분한) ≠ 겁에 질린. 감정 변조가 핵심 함정

questions.passage: There were obstacles to overcome and challenges to meet, but what adventure doesn't? I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges. All I needed to take with me was courage. I am already looking forward to my next trip in the future.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 글쓴이가 전달하려는 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 용기를 갖고 새로운 도전에 나서는 삶의 자세

det.korean: 용기(courage)로 새 세계에 뛰어들고 도전에 맞서자.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 용기+도전: 'All I needed was courage' + 'dove into a new world' + 'looking forward to my next trip'
❌ ① 안전 수칙: 부분적 에피소드(곰 만남)이지 전체 주제가 아님
❌ ② 편의시설: 케이블카 불가는 하나의 사건일 뿐
❌ ④ 감사: 마지막 문단에 언급되지만 핵심 메시지는 '용기'
det.tip: 마지막 문단의 핵심 문장: 'All I needed to take with me was courage.'

questions.passage: A month ago, I flew to San Francisco, feeling excited and a little scared. My only companions would be my best friend, Dan, and my wheelchair. There were obstacles to overcome and challenges to meet. I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges. All I needed to take with me was courage. I am already looking forward to my next trip in the future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: Wheels of Adventures: A Journey of Courage
San Francisco: The Best City for Tourists
How to Travel Safely with a Wheelchair

det.korean: 모험의 바퀴: 용기의 여정
det.analysis:
✅ ① Wheels of Adventures: 휠체어(wheels) + 모험(adventures) + 용기(courage)를 모두 포괄
❌ ② 관광 도시 소개가 아닌 개인 경험담
❌ ③ 여행 가이드가 아닌 감동적 여행기
❌ ④ 야생동물은 하나의 에피소드일 뿐
det.tip: 제목은 글 전체를 아우르는 키워드: wheels(휠체어), adventures(모험), courage(용기)

questions.passage: There were obstacles to overcome and challenges to meet, <u>but what adventure doesn't?</u> I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges. All I needed to take with me was courage.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "but what adventure doesn't?"가 함축하는 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 모험을 가지 않는 것이 더 현명하다.
어떤 모험이든 장애물과 도전은 있기 마련이다.
장애물이 없는 완벽한 모험을 찾아야 한다.

det.korean: "하지만 어떤 모험이 그렇지 않겠는가?" → 모든 모험에는 장애물과 도전이 있다는 의미의 수사 의문문.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 어떤 모험이든 도전은 있다: 수사 의문문으로 '모든 모험에 도전이 있다'는 보편적 진리를 표현
❌ ① 모험을 가지 말라: 오히려 도전을 긍정적으로 받아들이는 맥락
❌ ③ 특별히 많았다: '모든 모험'에 해당한다는 보편적 진술
❌ ④ 완벽한 모험: 장애물 없는 모험은 없다는 것이 핵심
det.tip: 수사 의문문(Rhetorical Question): 'What adventure doesn't (have obstacles)?' = 모든 모험에는 장애물이 있다

questions.passage: Our hike took a dangerous turn at one point. As we made our way down a trail, we encountered a black bear. I was so excited that I took out my camera to take a picture. It must have smelled the cold cuts and chips we had packed because <u>it</u> began to approach us. Thinking quickly, Uncle Roy grabbed a stone and threw it, yelling and waving.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 it이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 곰(the black bear)이 음식 냄새를 맡고 다가오기 시작했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① the black bear: 'encountered a black bear' → 'It must have smelled' → 'it began to approach us'. it은 곰을 지칭
❌ ② the camera: 카메라가 냄새를 맡거나 다가올 수 없음
❌ ③ the trail: 길이 다가올 수 없음
❌ ④ the picture: 사진이 행동할 수 없음
det.tip: 대명사 it의 선행사 찾기: 'smelled'(냄새 맡다)와 'approach'(다가오다)의 주어가 될 수 있는 것은 곰뿐

questions.passage: Dan found out that the National Park has a bike rental service and offers hand-crank bikes. Dan persuaded me to try one, and soon I was able to use the hand crank pretty well. We had a fun day riding along the trails in the park. The Tunnel View in Yosemite Valley was like a masterpiece painted by Mother Nature. The trail also led <u>us</u> to green fields and streams where we saw some wildlife.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 us가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글쓴이와 Dan이 자전거를 타고 공원의 오솔길을 따라 달렸다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 글쓴이와 Dan: 이 단락에서 자전거를 탄 것은 글쓴이와 Dan. 'Dan persuaded me to try one' → 'We had a fun day' → us
❌ ① Uncle Roy: 이 에피소드에서 Roy는 언급되지 않음
❌ ② Dan과 Roy: 글쓴이 본인이 핸드크랭크 자전거를 탔으므로 포함
❌ ④ 전체 방문객: 문맥상 둘만의 자전거 이야기
det.tip: 'Dan persuaded me'에서 me(글쓴이)와 Dan이 자전거 타기의 주체. us = 글쓴이 + Dan

questions.passage: Known for its rolling hills, the city has an extensive public transportation system. I was disappointed to find out that the historic cable cars, which I had been looking forward to riding, do not accommodate wheelchair users. Therefore, we decided to take a city tour bus with wheelchair access.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

글쓴이는 케이블카가 휠체어 사용자를 (          )하지 않는다는 것을 알게 되었다.

det.korean: 케이블카가 휠체어 사용자를 수용(accommodate)하지 않는다.
det.analysis: ✅ accommodate: 'do not accommodate wheelchair users'에서 핵심 동사
det.tip: accommodate(수용하다, 적응시키다) — '수용하다'의 의미로 wheelchair users와 함께 사용

questions.passage: We took a cruise, enjoying the view of the city. As we passed the bridge, the summer breeze blew slowly, and we watched the beautiful sunset. The next day, we traveled to Yosemite National Park, a place four hours away from San Francisco. The park is famous for Northern California's natural __________. (scene)
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 공원은 북부 캘리포니아의 자연 풍경(scenery)으로 유명하다.
det.analysis:
✅ scenery: scene(장면) → scenery(풍경, 경치). 자연 풍경을 나타내는 불가산 명사
❌ scenic: 형용사(경치 좋은)로 'natural scenic'은 부자연스러움
❌ scenes: 복수형은 '장면들'이라는 뜻으로 자연 풍경의 의미와 다름
det.tip: scene(장면, 가산) → scenery(풍경, 불가산). 'natural scenery'는 '자연 경치'라는 관용 표현

questions.passage: Thinking quickly, Uncle Roy grabbed a stone and threw it, yelling and waving. After turning me around, __________. Dan said, "I guess it's time to leave now."
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 알맞은 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)

[ Dan / helped / Uncle Roy / push / me / back / the way / we / came ]
questions.wa: Dan helped Uncle Roy push me back the way we came.
accept: Dan helped Uncle Roy push me back the way we came.
dan helped uncle roy push me back the way we came.
Dan helped Uncle Roy push me back the way we came
dan helped uncle roy push me back the way we came

det.korean: Dan은 Roy 삼촌이 나를 우리가 왔던 길로(the way we came) 밀어서 돌아가도록 도왔다(helped push).
det.analysis: ✅ 'Dan helped Uncle Roy push me back the way we came.' — 9단어. help + O + 원형부정사 + 부사 + 관계부사절
det.tip: help + 목적어 + 동사원형: helped Uncle Roy push. 'the way we came'은 관계부사 생략(the way in which we came)

questions.ans: Dan helped Uncle Roy push me back the way we came.

questions.stem:
다음 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.

[조건]
1. "우리는 공원의 오솔길을 따라 자전거를 타며 즐거운 하루를 보냈다."를 영어로 쓰시오.
2. 반드시 fun, riding, trails를 포함할 것.
3. 8단어 이상으로 쓸 것.
questions.wa: We had a fun day riding along the trails in the park.
accept: We had a fun day riding along the trails in the park.
We had a fun day riding along the trails in the park
we had a fun day riding along the trails in the park.
we had a fun day riding along the trails in the park

det.korean: 우리는 공원의 오솔길을 따라 자전거를 타며 즐거운 하루(a fun day)를 보냈다.
det.analysis: ✅ 'We had a fun day riding along the trails in the park.' — had a fun day ~ing: ~하며 즐거운 하루를 보냈다
det.tip: 'have a fun day ~ing'(~하며 즐거운 하루를 보내다). along the trails(오솔길을 따라)

questions.ans: We had a fun day riding along the trails in the park.

questions.stem:
다음 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.

[조건]
1. "나는 심호흡을 하고, 새로운 세계로 뛰어들어, 도전에 맞섰다."를 영어로 쓰시오.
2. 반드시 breath, dove, faced를 포함할 것.
3. 10단어 이상으로 쓸 것.
questions.wa: I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges.
accept: I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges.
I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges
i took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges.
i took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges

det.korean: 나는 심호흡(a deep breath)을 하고, 새로운 세계(a new world)로 뛰어들어(dove), 도전에 맞섰다(faced challenges).
det.analysis: ✅ 'I took a deep breath, dove into a new world, and faced challenges.' — 병렬구조(took, dove, faced) + 12단어
det.tip: 병렬구조: took, dove, faced — 모두 과거형. take a deep breath(심호흡하다), dove into(~로 뛰어들다)
